assumptions: The opportunity is judged at planning and pre-validation stage; absent private partner terms or pilot data are treated as uncertainty, while the documented incumbent offerings are treated as evidence.
The orchestrator does not develop a proprietary battery diagnostic, underwrite the guarantee, or carry claims risk; those functions remain with an authorized diagnostic or risk partner.
No exclusivity, non-circumvention protection, reseller margin, Polish guarantee authorization, or reusable data right exists unless and until it is contractually secured.
The founder remains employed, limits direct involvement to roughly 12-16 hours per week, and delegates vehicle testing and routine field execution to dealer staff or contractors.
No contribution revenue above an unproven reseller margin or implementation/support fee is credited, given the observed 250 PLN retail test reference and the provider's bundled guarantee positioning.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Battery uncertainty at used-EV intake and sale is a genuine transaction problem, and the legacy-fleet gap left by prospective battery passports supports a workflow need. However, the proposed insight has narrowed to local orchestration of an existing category: AVILOO already combines certification, APIs, and bounded protection, so the remaining Polish channel gap is plausible but not established as a structural opportunity.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A dealer has a credible reason to reduce battery-related uncertainty, discounts, and post-sale disputes, and AAA AUTO's several thousand tests plus its 250 PLN retail offer show real use of paid diagnostics. The missing question is incremental willingness to pay: there is no evidence that independent dealers will pay an additional orchestrator fee rather than buy directly from AVILOO, DEKRA, an OEM, or an insurer, nor evidence quantifying faster sales or avoided loss.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Keeping diagnostic and underwriting obligations with a partner makes the model capital-light, but it also leaves the venture with a thin reseller or implementation take rate. The 250 PLN consumer reference, a provider-positioned bundled guarantee, and unpriced field support, integrations, hardware logistics, and claims administration create margin pressure; no evidence establishes contribution margin, CAC, LTV, payback, cash conversion, or a credible path to the founder's wealth objective.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish mid-sized used-EV dealers, leasing remarketers, and auctions form a specific beachhead with a clear per-vehicle trigger, and a single-dealer pilot is appropriately narrow. Its economic size is unknown because eligible transaction volume by vehicle, warranty status, and model support is not evidenced, while a major Polish seller already uses an incumbent stack.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: AVILOO owns a validated diagnostic product, large comparative dataset, certificate, warranty API, and provider relationship, while DEKRA offers another trusted rapid certificate and AAA AUTO demonstrates local deployment. Without exclusive channel rights or ownership of the dealer relationship, the orchestrator has no demonstrated control point from which to dominate even the initial segment.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful dealer workflow could extend to lease returns, auctions, additional diagnostic or warranty providers, claims analytics, and nearby CEE markets. Those adjacencies are logically available, but each still depends on external permissions and provider economics, and the current wedge does not yet create a proprietary asset that makes expansion materially easier.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Dealer integrations, localized eligibility rules, and claims operations could create modest workflow embeddedness. The candidate has no proven exclusivity, proprietary diagnostic, protected data rights, or durable dealer ownership; the upstream provider can contract directly, and broader regulatory access plus battery passports may commoditize basic health evidence.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Localization and one integrated ordering-to-claims workflow may improve convenience for an underserved dealer. There is no evidence of a meaningful advantage in price, diagnostic quality, speed, trust, coverage, outcome, or data versus direct AVILOO or DEKRA access and the already bundled AAA AUTO offer.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The Data Act, battery-health access requirements, the future passport regime, and AVILOO's staged guarantee rollout make 2026 a reasonable moment to test an integration layer for legacy vehicles. The same forces also improve upstream access and standardization, and capable incumbents are already active, so timing creates a window for validation rather than a clear first-mover advantage.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The partner-first plan followed by one dealer-group pilot is concrete and compatible with focused B2B selling rather than a founder-led media brand. Yet access to the product itself is the first distribution gate, partner willingness and economics are unknown, established providers can sell directly, and there is no evidence of repeatable acquisition cost or dealer conversion.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and automation skills fit integrations and workflow software, and outsourcing tests while a licensed partner bears technical and risk obligations makes a part-time pilot feasible. Execution still hinges on obtaining partner rights, resolving Polish warranty or insurance-distribution requirements, supporting variable vehicle coverage, administering claims, and preventing disintermediation, all within the founder's limited weekly capacity.

main_structural_strength: A provider-authorized, dealer-embedded workflow can be piloted with limited capital and lets a specialized partner carry diagnostic validation and guarantee risk while the founder applies automation and integration skills to a recurring per-vehicle process.
primary_score_limiter: The venture lacks an owned control point: one upstream provider can determine product access, Polish eligibility, margin, data rights, and guarantee terms while also being able to bypass the orchestrator and contract directly with dealers.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: AVILOO already offers the rapid certificate, authorized API surface, and one-year/20,000-kilometre EUR 3,000 guarantee contemplated by the concept, while AAA AUTO already deploys AVILOO testing in Poland from 250 PLN and bundles certification, re-testing, and battery protection; DEKRA adds a second established rapid-certificate competitor.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Written partner terms must establish Polish warranty availability, attractive per-vehicle and recurring software margin, lead or account protection, non-circumvention, and reusable data rights. A dealer pilot must then show incremental willingness to pay, supported eligible volume, measurable reduction in days-to-sale, discounting or disputes, repeat usage, acquisition cost, contribution margin, payback, and a compliant claims arrangement.
highest_value_structural_change: Convert the single-provider reseller into a dealer-contracted, provider-neutral battery transaction operating layer that normalizes OEM and third-party evidence, owns the intake-to-listing-to-re-test workflow, charges recurring per-location software plus transaction fees, and retains contractually permitted longitudinal derived data; use licensed partners only for diagnostics and protection, with explicit non-circumvention and account ownership.
